thread.title: South Korea to Hold Snap Presidential Election on June 3
thread.title_full: South Korea to Hold Snap Presidential Election on June 3

author: NDT Bureau
title: South Korea to Hold Snap Presidential Election on June 3
text:
• South Korea will hold a snap presidential election on June 3.
• The election is to choose a successor to ousted President Yoon Suk Yeol.
• Yoon was removed from office by the Constitutional Court for imposing martial law.
• The law mandates an election within 60 days of a president's removal.
• The next president will serve a full 5-year term.
• The election is expected to be a two-way contest between the People Power Party and the Democratic Party.
• The Democratic Party currently holds a majority in the National Assembly.
• The People Power Party faces challenges in restoring public confidence and addressing internal divisions.
• Lee Jae-myung is expected to be the Democratic Party candidate and is considered the front-runner.
• Primaries for presidential candidates are expected to be launched in the coming weeks.
• Lee narrowly lost the 2022 election to Yoon and has faced no major challengers within his party.
• Yoon's decision to enact martial law has negatively impacted the reputation of the People Power Party.
• Some members of the People Power Party criticized Yoon's actions and voted for his impeachment.
• Yoon has loyal supporters who believe he is a victim of a leftist opposition.
• Experts suggest the conservative party faces significant disadvantages in the upcoming election.
• The current leadership of the People Power Party is filled with Yoon loyalists.
• Labor Minister Kim Moon Soo is considered the most pro-Yoon candidate among the hopefuls.
• Lee Jae-myung faces five ongoing trials for corruption and other charges.
• If elected, Lee would gain presidential immunity from these trials.
• Yoon has accused the Democratic Party of obstructing his agenda and undermining his presidency.
